name: Sanctuary on Potomac
award: 2024 Federal 9% and state housing tax credits (Round One)
headline: The Aurora Housing Authority is building Sanctuary on Potomac, a 43-unit permanent supportive housing building for people leaving homelessness who have mental illness, on Aurora Mental Health and Recovery's Potomac campus at 1280 S. Potomac St. Every unit has a project-based voucher. It won $1,408,140 a year in federal 9% credit and $700,000 in state credit in CHFA's 2024 Round One.
why_it_matters: It puts supportive housing on the same campus as a 24-hour crisis and detox center, with clinical case management from the mental health center and services paid partly from a $235,000 tenant services reserve funded by a CHFA cost basis waiver, a structure other housing authorities can copy.

status.label: Under construction: building permit issued 2025-05-28; no certificate of occupancy found
status.detail: Aurora's permit data show the 43-unit building permit applied for 2024-12-23 and issued 2025-05-28, a construction trailer permit in July 2025 and plan revisions through 2026-10-12. In April 2025 the housing authority told a city committee that construction was underway with completion expected in August 2026; its website still says "Coming 2026", and Aurora's 2026 certificate of occupancy layer has no entry for 1280 S. Potomac St.

next_step: Watch Aurora's certificate of occupancy data for 1280 S. Potomac St. and the housing authority's site for an opening date.

background.text: Campus model: the building is part of Aurora Mental Health and Recovery's Potomac campus, which also holds a 24-hour crisis center and detox center, with a community health clinic planned; the mental health center assembled $7.0M, $5.0M and $1.3M in ARPA money from Aurora, Arapahoe County and Adams County for the campus (about $13.3M in all, inferred sum).

Second try: the project applied in CHFA's 2023 Round Two with the same 43 units and AMI split. Between rounds it added $1.2M from Arapahoe County, won Planning Commission site plan approval and recorded a parking easement.

Local approvals: the Aurora Planning and Zoning Commission recommended the site plan for approval at a public hearing on 2023-11-21 with no public opposition registered; the campus infrastructure site plan was submitted in June 2023. A HUD environmental assessment was done by City of Aurora staff and the old building on the site was demolished.

Cost drivers: the parcel only fits 43 units, so per-unit cost is high; the applicant also cites full-time on-site staff, overnight security and extra architectural detail the city required because the building does not front Potomac.

Market: the study found 572 people homeless in Aurora in the 2023 point-in-time count and only 108 PSH units in the city (Renaissance Veterans Apartments at Fitzsimons and Providence at the Heights); it projected a two-month lease-up.

Permits: Aurora's permit data list the 43-unit multifamily building permit (24-2498416-000-00, valuation $10,000,000) issued 2025-05-28, followed by fire sprinkler (2025-10), fire alarm (2025-11) and emergency radio (2026-01) sub-permits and structural RFI confirmation of as-built conditions in April 2026.
